2016_099_092016mtg.paragraph: Agenda packet for the Troy Board of Education regular meeting of September 20, 2016 at the Services Building. It carries the July 2016 Treasurer's Report with total disbursements in period of $8,904,171.60, four new teacher hires, the September enrollment count of 12,817 students against 12,670 a year earlier, a $198,325.00 food service equipment award to Great Lakes Hotel Supply Company, and a five-year Troy Career Center lease to Robbins Investment, LLC at $104,916.00 in the first year. Reports cover professional development, technology, enrollment and the 2013 bond program's Series 1 construction.
2016_099_092016mtg.page:
**Meeting**
Regular meeting, September 20, 2016, 7:00 PM, Services Building, 4420 Livernois.

**Recognition**
Mr. Jolly reads biographies of the seventeen Spring 2016 All-State Athletes, drawn from boys and girls lacrosse, girls tennis, girls soccer, girls track and boys golf at both high schools. The Mission Moment honors four sixth-grade students from the 2016 Summer Success Academy — a four-week program helping fifth graders transition to middle school through four hours a day of math and language arts — introduced by teacher Kim Cornelisson. ASBO International's Certificate of Excellence in Financial Reporting is presented for the Comprehensive Annual Financial Report for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2015, recognizing Rick West and his staff. The Michigan Association of School Boards presents the Board with its Honor Board achievement and a Standard of Excellence Award, with Vice President Karl Schmidt receiving the Award of Distinction, Trustee Todd Miletti the Master Board Member Award, and Secretary Paula Fleming recognized for sixteen years of service. Four student representatives are introduced: Ellory Thill (Athens), Aman Agrawal (IA-East), Pranathi Locula (Troy High) and Parker Gilchrist (Troy College & Career).

**Treasurer's Report — July 2016**
Check disbursements total $6,539,129.74 — General Fund $3,822,749.72, Special Revenue Funds $612,834.27 and Other Funds $2,103,545.75 — with ACH debits of $8,957.53, outgoing wire transfers of $2,301,113.01, P-Card purchases of $55,985.16 and prior period voids of ($1,013.84), giving total disbursements in period of $8,904,171.60. Building & Site Funds account for 2,082,466.59 of the total and the Food Service Fund 559,180.53.

**Personnel and reports**
Four probationary contracts are recommended: Amina Taqi (.4 ELL, Baker), Brian Meade (Science, Boulan Park), Carrie Hodge (Kindergarten, Morse) and John Sheehan (Math, Troy High), each with a biographical sketch. Jordan Harris gives the staffing update; Teaching & Learning reports on professional development and a technology update follow.

The enrollment update from Mark Dziatczak and Kris Griffor compares September 15, 2015 with September 20, 2016:

| Level | 2015 | 2016 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Elementary (incl. Early Childhood Niles) | 5,515 | 5,542 |
| Middle schools | 2,903 | 2,988 |
| High schools and transition programs | 4,252 | 4,287 |
| **Total students** | **12,670** | **12,817** |

Boulan Park shows the largest single gain, 775 to 828, and Bemis the largest decline, 570 to 521.

**Business**
8.A awards BID 9826, food service equipment and installation, to Great Lakes Hotel Supply Company at $198,325.00 from the 2016-2017 Food Services Fund — seven Hobart M15T-2 dishwashers at $13,834.00 each for $96,838.00, plus single units for Costello, Smith, Athens and Troy High including a conveyor dishwasher at $25,312.00 and a combi oven at $10,662.00. Five bidders were invited and four responded; the competing totals were $200,204.00, $207,779.10 and $215,340.00.

8.B awards a five-year Troy Career Center lease to Robbins Investment, LLC, reviewed with Denise VanHee of Oakland County Michigan Works!. Robbins bid $104,916.00 for 2016-17 on 7,494 square feet at $14.00 per square foot, rising to $112,410.00 at $15.00 per square foot by 2020-21; the competing proposal from Thomas Duke Company ranged from $147,000.00 to $184,000.00 at $21.00 to $23.00 per square foot. Bid amounts exclude monthly electric.

**Other**
The Board certifies Paula Fleming, Todd Miletti, Nancy Philippart and Karl Schmidt as delegates to the MASB 2016 Delegate Assembly, November 10-13, 2016. Rick West presents the 2013 Bond Program Series 1 construction update prepared with Barton Malow and TMP, covering the 2016 projects: Bid Package 8 for mechanical and electrical upgrades and bathroom renovations at Athens and pool dehumidification, gym lights and chiller replacement at Troy High; Bid Package 16 for the International Academy's locker room conversion to classrooms, window replacement and mechanical/electrical upgrades along with mechanical, electrical and door work at Hamilton Elementary; and Bid Package 17 for paving replacement and site lighting at Athens, Troy High, Smith and Schroeder. A OneTroy report for the 2016/2017 school year closes the agenda.
2016_099_092016mtg.verbose:
Agenda packet for the regular meeting of the Troy School District Board of Education, September 20, 2016, 7:00 PM at the Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098. The agenda is: 1. Pledge of Allegiance; 2. Recognition (items A through E); 3. Additions & Deletions; 4. Public Communication (agenda items); 5. General – Consent Agenda; 6. Personnel; 7. Curriculum; 8. Business; 9. Public Communication (non-agenda items); 10. Other; 11. Adjournment. Meetings are cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) every Monday and Wednesday at 2:00 and 9:00 p.m. when school is in session, and viewable at http://vimeo.com/troyschools.

**Recognition.** Item 2.A names the All-State Athletes for Spring 2016, with Mr. Jolly reading biographies: Blake Best (Senior, Troy High, boys lacrosse), Hannah Cimpeanu (Junior, Troy High, girls tennis), Jordan Coval (Junior, Troy High, boys lacrosse), Deepthi Devireddy (Senior, Troy High, girls tennis), Lauren Fulcher (Freshman, Troy High, girls track), Mitchell Gorski (Junior, Athens, boys lacrosse), Amanda Harris (Senior, Athens, girls soccer), Jacob Lining (Junior, Athens, boys lacrosse), Ashley Leonard (Junior, Athens, girls soccer), Morgan MacDonald (Freshman, Troy High, girls lacrosse), Justin Parry (Junior, Troy High, boys lacrosse), Leena Penumalee (Senior, Troy High, girls tennis), Hannah Schell (Senior, Athens, girls soccer), Kate Schabet (Senior, Troy High, girls lacrosse), Logan Shamblin (Senior, Troy High, boys lacrosse), Dennis Volostnykh (Senior, Athens, boys golf) and Megan Worrel (Sophomore, Troy High, girls track).

Item 2.B is a TSD Mission Moment on the 2016 Summer Success Academy, honoring four sixth-grade students for their effort, attitude and learning. SSA teacher Kim Cornelisson introduces the program: a four-week course designed to help fifth grade students transition successfully to middle school, with lead teacher Jason Fawcett unable to attend and teachers Sree Bollavaram and Angela Correa present. The students recognized are Jonathan Shields (Baker Middle School), Julia Williams (Boulan Park Middle School), Hannah Dempsey (Larson Middle School) and Jack Cooper (Smith Middle School), each of whom spent four hours a day developing a growth mindset, improving math skills and understanding of math concepts, and applying language arts skills and strategies; the script notes they exceeded individual expectations and contributed positively to their learning communities.

Item 2.C presents the Association of School Business Officials International's Certificate of Excellence in Financial Reporting, honoring the district for its Comprehensive Annual Financial Report for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2015 and recognizing Rick West, Assistant Superintendent for Business Services, and his staff. The certificate is signed by Brenda R. Burkett, CPA, CSBA, SFO, President, and John D. Musso, CAE, RSBA, Executive Director. A March 22, 2016 letter from Musso to West conveys the award and notes that the Certificate of Excellence Review Team's comments must be addressed in the following year's CAFR, with written responses required as part of the next application packet. The attached press release, issued from Reston, VA, describes the award as sponsored by VALIC — the first company to enroll a K-12 public school district in a 403(b) plan, with more than $86 billion in total assets under management as of June 30, 2015 and plans for nearly 24,000 groups serving nearly 1.8 million participants — and notes ASBO International was founded in 1910 and has 5,000 members.

The attached review comments, dated March 17, 2016, record the Review Team's consensus to award the Certificate and compliment the district on a high quality CAFR, while listing five items: the transmittal letter should include population, number of students, projected enrollment and the age of school buildings (noted in the prior year); only amounts with externally imposed restrictions should be reported as restricted (noted in the prior year); the reconciliation of operating income to net cash from operating activities does not agree to the cash flows from operating activities; the Statement of Changes in Fiduciary Assets and Liabilities should be placed in the combining and individual fund statements section (noted in the prior year); and information about principal property taxpayers and principal employers should be presented for the current fiscal period and the period ended nine years prior (noted in the prior two years). GASB updates are appended as a courtesy, covering Statements 72 through 77 on fair value measurement, pensions outside GASB 68, postemployment benefit plans other than pensions, the GAAP hierarchy and tax abatement disclosures.

Item 2.D presents Michigan Association of School Boards awards: the Board's Honor Board achievement and Standard of Excellence Award, the Award of Distinction for Vice President Karl Schmidt, the Master Board Member Award for Trustee Todd Miletti, and recognition of Secretary Paula Fleming for serving sixteen years on the Board. Item 2.E introduces the student representatives. Ellory Thill is a senior at Athens with a 4.05 GPA, an AP scholar and scholar athlete active in Student Council, National Honors Society, Interact, S.A.D.D., Ethnic Club and DECA, who played a large role in a Charity Week that raised over $84,000 for the Joan Rose Foundation and hopes to study education. Aman Agrawal is a junior at International Academy-East, three years on student council and currently Vice President, active in Yearbook Club and IA-East's buildOn student leadership board. Pranathi Locula is a senior at Troy High, captain of the tennis team and a member of the swim team, math team, HOSA and National Honors Society, who qualified for the HOSA international competition and took fifth place. Parker Gilchrist is a senior dual enrolled at Troy College & Career High School and Oakland Community College, a member of Student Government who has organized Field Day with Niles Center preschoolers, a holiday coat drive and a blood drive, raised money for the Water for Lebanon Project, and belongs to Women of Tomorrow, the Leadership and Social Justice teams and the Fingers Crossed Theater Troupe.

**Consent agenda.** Minutes of the August 16, 2016 Board meeting, minutes of the August 24, 2016 special workshop, and the Treasurer's Report for July 2016.

**Treasurer's Report, July 2016.** Rick West transmits the check register including current period voids, ACH debits, wire transfers and P-Card purchases, certifying the disbursements were payments for district obligations and that materials or services were received or performed. By fund: General Fund (101) 3,776,328.11; Grant Fund (120) 8,789.63; Special Education Fund (122) 37,631.98; Durant Funds (140) none — a General Fund total of $3,822,749.72. Food Service Fund (520) 559,180.53; Troy Career Center (529) 11,072.66; Community Education Fund (530) 42,581.08; Facilities Rental Fund (535) none — Special Revenue Funds totalling $612,834.27. Debt Funds none; Building & Site Funds (499, 414) 2,082,466.59; Student Activity Fund (700, 701) 21,079.16; Memorial Scholarship Fund (750) none — Other Funds totalling $2,103,545.75. Total check disbursements are $6,539,129.74; with ACH debits of $8,957.53, outgoing wire transfers of $2,301,113.01, P-Card purchases of $55,985.16 and prior period void disbursements of ($1,013.84), total disbursements in period are $8,904,171.60.

**Personnel.** Item 6.A recommends probationary contracts for four teachers with biographical sketches: Amina Taqi, .4 ELL Teacher at Baker Middle School, an Oakland University M.A. who taught in Novi and student taught at Hamilton Elementary, resident of Troy; Brian Meade, 1.0 Science Teacher at Boulan Park, a Wayne State M.E. who taught in Clawson Public Schools, resident of Macomb; Carrie Hodge, 1.0 Kindergarten Teacher at Morse Elementary, previously at Prevail Academy in Mt. Clemens with student teaching at King-Westwood Elementary, resident of Oxford; and John Sheehan, 1.0 Math Teacher at Troy High School, previously at Bishop Foley Catholic High School in Madison Heights, resident of Troy. Item 6.B is a staffing update presented by Jordan Harris.

**Curriculum reports.** Item 7.A is a Teaching & Learning professional development report; 7.B a technology update; and 7.C the enrollment update from Mark Dziatczak, Deputy Superintendent of Teaching and Learning, and Kris Griffor, Assistant Superintendent for Elementary Instruction, comparing September 15, 2015 with September 20, 2016. Elementary: Barnard 466 then 488; Bemis 570 then 521; Costello 340 then 359; Hamilton 482 then 509; Hill 328 then 324; Leonard 458 then 435; Martell 492 then 503; Morse 454 then 464; Schroeder 521 then 514; Troy Union 475 then 472; Wass 431 then 426; Wattles 461 then 492; Early Childhood Niles 37 then 35; total 5,515 then 5,542. Middle schools: Baker 735 then 736; Boulan Park 775 then 828; Larson 697 then 726; Smith 696 then 698; total 2,903 then 2,988. High schools: Athens 1,573 then 1,578; Troy 1,982 then 1,983; IAE 533 then 556; Troy College & Career 112 then 103; Troy Center for Transition/Search 52 then 67; total 4,252 then 4,287. Total students 12,670 then 12,817.

**Business: food service equipment.** Item 8.A awards food services equipment and installation to Great Lakes Hotel Supply Company in the amount of $198,325.00 as an expenditure of the 2016-2017 Food Services Fund. Todd Hensley's August 31, 2016 memorandum on BID 9826 records that invitations went to five potential bidders with four responding, none of them a no-bid, and that after analysis with Gayle Moran, Director/General Manager of Food Service for Sodexo, Great Lakes Hotel Supply was the lowest qualified bidder. The award covers seven Hobart M15T-2 dishwashers at $13,834.00 each, extending to $96,838.00, for Barnard, Bemis, Hamilton, Martell, Schroeder, Troy Union and Wass elementary schools; one Hobart AM15T dishwasher at $14,437.00 for Costello; one Hobart AM15T-2 at $13,834.00 for Smith Middle School; a Convection Steamer SX-55 at $14,154.00 for Athens; a Convection Steamer GSX-10 plus Bakers Pride GDCO-G2 at $23,088.00 and a Combi Oven XAVC-1011 at $10,662.00 for Troy High; and a conveyor dishwasher CL44E at $25,312.00. The tabulation shows competing totals of $207,779.10 from Douglas Equipment, $215,340.00 from Gold Star Products and $200,204.00 from Stafford Smith, Inc. against Great Lakes Hotel Supply's $198,325.00.

**Business: Troy Career Center lease.** Item 8.B awards a five-year lease to Robbins Investment, LLC, with authorization for the Superintendent or designee to execute the agreement. Hensley's August 31, 2016 memorandum on RFP 9825, professional office space for the Troy location of the Michigan Works! program, records invitations to four potential bidders with two responding, reviewed with Denise VanHee, Assistant Manager of Oakland County Michigan Works! Troy. The tabulation gives Robbins Investments LLC $104,916.00 for 2016-17 on 7,494 square feet at $14.00 per square foot, $106,789.50 at $14.25 for 2017-18, $108,663.00 at $14.50 for 2018-19, $110,536.50 at $14.75 for 2019-20 and $112,410.00 at $15.00 for 2020-21; Thomas Duke Company proposed ranges of $147,000.00 to $168,000.00 at $21.00 per square foot in the first year rising to $161,000.00 to $184,000.00 at $23.00 in the last, on 7,000 to 8,000 square feet. All bid amounts exclude monthly electric expenses.

**Other.** Item 10.A certifies Paula Fleming, Todd Miletti, Nancy Philippart and Karl Schmidt as delegates to the Michigan Association of School Boards' 2016 Delegate Assembly during the MASB Fall Conference, November 10-13, 2016, allowing them to make motions and vote; Paula Fleming signs the certification. Item 10.B is Rick West's bond update, a 2013 Bond Program Series 1 construction update for September 2016 prepared with Barton Malow and TMP. The 2016 construction projects are Bid Package 8 at Athens and Troy High School — mechanical and electrical upgrades and bathroom renovations at Athens, and pool dehumidification, gym lights and chiller replacement at Troy High; Bid Package 16 at the International Academy and Hamilton Elementary — locker room conversion to classrooms, window replacement and mechanical and electrical upgrades at IAE, and mechanical and electrical upgrades and door replacement at Hamilton; and Bid Package 17 at Athens, Troy High, Smith Middle School and Schroeder Elementary — paving replacement and site lighting upgrades. Photographs document the Troy High chiller installation and pool dehumidification upgrades, Athens mechanical upgrades and bathroom renovations, and gymnasium lighting upgrades at both high schools. Item 10.C is a OneTroy report for the 2016/2017 school year.
